headline: All majors below the 200-day; mixed momentum signals with expensive shorts lining up in altcoins while whales pull Bitcoin into cold storage.
paragraphs: The regime is unambiguous: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none have established a golden cross. That is a downtrend in the technical definition, regardless of the day-to-day noise. Bitcoin sits 47.8% below its 12-month high of $124,739; Ethereum is 60.1% down from $4,817; Solana has fallen 68.8% from $247.60; and the outlier wreckage is Doge at 75.7% off $0.2893. The price action over the last week and month, though, tells a different story than the longer structure suggests. Bitcoin up 0.59% in seven days and 8.69% in thirty; Ethereum up 0.11% and 22.2%; Solana up 3.59% and 9.64%; BNB up 2.79% and 9.24%. These are not the moves of a market in free fall. They are the moves of a market resting above a crater.

Momentum is split between assets and shows a subtle divergence from price. Bitcoin's RSI sits at 56, above the midline but not extended; its MACD is above signal, suggesting gentle upward lean. Ethereum's RSI is 57.3 and its MACD is below signal, a small red flag when price is stable. Solana's RSI is 57.8 with MACD above, aligned. The story shifts at BNB, which has an RSI of 66.2 (pushing into overbought) with MACD above signal, suggesting a short-term pulse that has moved ahead of the longer trend. Cardano is the outlier: RSI at 66.2 with MACD above signal, but the asset has risen 36% in thirty days and 16% in seven days from a base that is 79.5% below its 12-month high. That is a technical bounce, not a reversal of regime. XRP's RSI sits at 40.7 with MACD below signal and the price down 3.95% over seven days; it is the one major that is quietly deteriorating while the crowd watches elsewhere.

Derivatives positioning reveals a market where longs are paying to hold the bet and shorts are bunched up in the smaller names, vulnerable. Bitcoin's funding rate stands at 0.67% per eight hours, annualized to 7.3%, with open interest at $2.09 billion and a long-to-short ratio of 1.14. That is a mild premium to hold longs, neither expensive nor cheap. Ethereum's funding is lower at 0.21% annualized to 2.3%, with 1.33 longs per short, still tilted long. Solana's funding jumps to 0.84% annualized to 9.2% with a 2.01 ratio, the first sign of crowding. But the real crowding lives in the smaller caps: XRP has an 11% annualized rate and a 3.61 long-to-short ratio; Doge has 11% annualized and a 4.99 ratio. In the last 21 hours, XRP has liquidated $327,179 in longs against only $28,488 in shorts; Doge liquidated $134,275 longs against $4,368 shorts. The shorts are scarce and the longs are packed. A reversal in either name would find very little buying interest on the way down.

Whale behavior over the last 48 hours shows a net outflow of $103 million, all of it Bitcoin leaving exchanges. The breakdown is stark: $168 million in Bitcoin has moved off exchanges, offset by $65 million onto Binance. Kraken alone has shipped out $117.9 million and $50 million in separate moves. This is the classic accumulation signal: large holders moving coins to cold storage while retail sentiment sits in Fear territory at 31 on the Greed Index, within its 30-day range of 22 to 33. The stablecoin float sits at $306.2 billion, down 1.02% over the month, a slow leak rather than a panic withdrawal. ETF flows on the traditional finance side have been persistent: Bitcoin net inflows of $101.7 million on 07 Aug, with all five recent sessions in the same direction and a cumulative $865.3 million inflow over the window. Ethereum has seen $49.6 million on the same date with four of five sessions aligned, cumulative $243.7 million. The signal is tidy: institutions are buying spot while whales pull supply off the market, but price is resting, not accelerating.

Fear dominates sentiment while the tape whispers the opposite. The Greed Index at 31 reflects the long drawdown; the total market cap is up only 0.22% in 24 hours, and Bitcoin dominance sits steady at 56.7%, neither capitulating to altcoins nor collapsing further. The top movers show scattered retail interest: BEAT up 35.1%, PUMP up 12.9%, the names that chase. The losers are the established plays, ENA, AERO, and CRO down low single digits. That is noise, not a narrative. Network difficulty will retarget in 1,882 blocks, down 1.6% from the last period, a cooling of mining hash as economics remain tight. Bitcoin fees are at 1 sat per byte, the slowest possible, suggesting transaction volume is light and urgency is absent.

Watch for three conditions that would signal a regime shift. First, a reclaim of the 200-day moving average by Bitcoin or Ethereum would break the downtrend structure; the longer the prices stay below, the less likely a single day's burst will hold. Second, any acceleration of outflows from Kraken or other major exchanges combined with price that breaks above resistance would suggest the whale accumulation is turning into forced short covering. Third, monitor the funding rates on XRP and Doge, which are now at 11% annualized with extreme long positioning; any sudden liquidation cascade that clears shorts fast rather than slowly grinding them out would signal a washout of the current setup. Until then, the tape reads as a bear market at rest, with smart money loading while the crowd waits for permission to care.
